axes.model_access:
Anthropic's own Claude family.

**v2.1.284 (2026-09-28) added Claude Sonnet 5.5 (`claude-sonnet-5-5`).
The official notes it is the default Sonnet model on the Anthropic API.**
Spec is 1M context (API pricing on the official pricing page; not stored by this site).
axes.runtime:
A local process running in the terminal; its lifetime is bound to the terminal session.
The repository contains `.devcontainer`, indicating support for containerized dev environments.
axes.local_files:
**The permission model is strongly tied to the working directory** —

the CHANGELOG records that auto mode asks "before reading files outside the working directories".
It also added a "Yes, but ask again next time" option.
That means: allow this one read, and keep asking afterwards.

1M context tier (see model_access).
axes.background:
**The terminal form needs a resident client, but the official has a cloud form that keeps running after shutdown.**

Official `claude-code-on-the-web` wording:
"A cloud session is a Claude Code session that runs on cloud
infrastructure instead of on your machine... The session keeps
running after you close your laptop."

The CLI creates a cloud session with `claude --cloud` (the old `--remote` is an alias),
and `claude --teleport` pulls a cloud session back into the terminal to continue;

Routines (created in the CLI via `/schedule`) run on Anthropic-managed cloud,
**official wording**: "they keep working when your laptop is closed".

Cloud sessions and routines require a paid Pro / Max / Team or Enterprise seat.

Quotas and limits follow the plan. The official routines page has a standalone "Usage and limits" section.
axes.tools:
**MCP support is complete and continuously strengthening** —

v2.1.284 added `/mcp reconnect all`. It retries all failed-or-unauthenticated MCP servers in one shot.

The same version fixed an issue: on session resume, MCP tool calls reported "No such tool available"
while the server was actually still connecting. It now **waits up to 10 seconds**.
axes.context:
**The context-compaction mechanism has explicit boundary handling** —

v2.1.284 fixed a persistent error: when the request is still too long after compacting,
it kept reporting "Prompt is too long". It now **compacts once more, keeping less of the recent conversation**.

That shows it genuinely has multi-round compaction, and edge cases are being patched continuously.
axes.fit:
Users who value controllable permissions, need the MCP ecosystem, and want Anthropic's official models.
**Not a fit for scenarios needing an open-source license or self-hosting** (the license is explicitly proprietary).

sections.⚠ 许可状态（最重要的前提）:
`LICENSE.md` original text:

> © Anthropic PBC. **All rights reserved.**
> Use is subject to Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service.

**This is not an open-source license.** The GitHub API's license field returning `NONE` is for the same reason.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Can I read the source? | Yes (the repository is public) |
| Can I use it commercially? | Must follow Anthropic's Commercial Terms |
| Can I distribute it closed-source? | **No** (All rights reserved) |
| Can I self-host? | Not applicable (proprietary + subscription) |

**This must be made clear before any selection decision** —
"the tool is on GitHub" does not equal "you are free to use it".

sections.权限设计：本分区最细:
### ① Asks per path, with an "allow just this once"

v2.1.284 added an option:

```
Added a "Yes, but ask again next time" answer to auto mode's prompt
before a read outside the working directories, so you can allow that one
read and still be asked about later ones
```

**This design deserves its own record**. Most tools' approvals have only two states — allow / deny.
Claude Code offers a third state: **allow this once, but keep asking**.

It resolves a real dilemma:

- allow globally → lose the protection
- confirm every time → workflow interruptions

### ② Managed policies control usable models

```
Added Claude apps gateway startup warnings when a managed policy's
availableModels is empty, or leaves out the model Claude Code starts on
without setting model or enforceAvailableModels
```

In enterprise scenarios:

- usable models are controlled by the `availableModels` policy
- `enforceAvailableModels` decides whether it is enforced
- **policy mismatches warn at startup** — no silent degradation

### ③ Quota visibility

```
Added dollar amounts to the Claude apps gateway spend limit in /usage
and the status line
```

`/usage` and the status line show **concrete spend numbers** rather than abstract percentages (the original example contains amounts; not quoted per D9 policy).
sections.MCP 支持在持续加强:
Both v2.1.284 changes concern MCP:

| Change | Content |
|---|---|
| added | `/mcp reconnect all` — retry all failed or unauthenticated servers in one shot |
| fixed | on session resume MCP tools reported "No such tool available" (the server was actually still connecting); it now **waits up to 10 seconds** |

**The value of the second fix**: it reveals a real scenario —
**a race exists between session resume and MCP server connection**.
Only heavy usage would surface this class of problem.
sections.上下文压缩的边界处理:
```
Fixed "Prompt is too long" errors that persisted after compacting:
when the compacted request is still too long, Claude Code now compacts
once more, keeping less of the recent conversation
```

**What this shows**: after compaction a request may still be too long; then it **compacts once more** and **keeps less of the recent conversation**.

This is honest boundary handling — not pretending one compaction solves everything.
